headline: SafeWebWorld finds plausible web-agent predictions can still omit authorization evidence
summary: A 29 Oct 2026 arXiv preprint introduces SafeWebWorld, a five-domain benchmark asking whether predicted web actions preserve evidence needed to choose among Execute, Ask, and Block. The authors report that 86.1% of 3,000 matched predictions from ten frozen open models were judged semantically plausible, while plausibility and low false-safe rates could coexist with weak evidence recovery or poor Ask recall. These are author-reported results on constructed cases: one primary reviewer audited the frozen test set, shortcut features remain predictive, and live action outcomes were not tested.
